title: KMS rotation: enterprise customer expectations + documentation deliverables for security reviews
creator: Naomi Feldman
project: Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs
description:
Summary
Enterprise prospects/customers (especially regulated) are consistently asking for: (1) a clear rotation cadence policy, (2) a step-by-step rotation procedure they can operationalize, and (3) evidence artifacts they can hand to auditors (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / internal). This ticket defines customer-facing expectations and the documentation/evidence deliverables Product needs from Eng/Security/Docs so Sales/SE are not generating bespoke narratives.

Background / signals
- Acme Bank security review (Fireflies 2025-11-06): asked for rotation cadence, outage behavior, and “what proof do we get that rotation occurred and who approved it?”
- Northpeak Health deep dive (Fireflies 2025-11-13): asked for Private deployment operator steps, IAM/KMS permission minimums, and troubleshooting for AccessDenied/Throttling.
- Support cases: SUP-19405 (rotation cutover questions + evidence request), SUP-19341 (AccessDenied), SUP-19377 (throttling -> elevated 5xx).

Customer expectations (what we should be able to say consistently)
1) Cadence
- Default recommendation: rotate Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) at least annually; quarterly is preferred for regulated customers with stricter internal policy.
- Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) are short-lived/ephemeral where possible; if a component persists DEKs for envelope encryption, that DEK rotation behavior must be documented per component (and supported by dual-read/cutover where applicable).
- Redwood supports customer-managed cadence for Private and Dedicated, provided the platform receives the new key version and a cutover window is followed.
- Exceptions: If a customer cannot rotate on schedule (vendor change freeze, regulatory audit period), we need an explicit exception request path + compensating controls.

2) Responsibility split (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Hosted API: Redwood operates the control plane and rotation procedure; customers receive evidence via audit logs/exports and a rotation record (on request / via standard export).
- Dedicated: Similar to Hosted, but with customer-specific KMS configuration and potentially customer-owned keys; Redwood runs the procedure unless contract requires customer execution.
- Private: Customer owns the KMS/HSM and IAM policies; Redwood provides operator procedure, validation tooling (installer preflight + health checks), and evidence templates. Customer executes (or executes jointly with Redwood PS depending on contract).

3) What happens during rotation (behavioral guarantees)
- No plaintext exposure; envelope encryption stays intact.
- Rotation is staged:
  a) Introduce new key version (no cutover yet)
  b) Enable dual-decrypt/dual-read window (decrypt old+new) so reads remain available
  c) Cutover for new writes (encrypt with new) once health checks and success criteria are met
  d) Disable old key version only after a defined burn-in period and verification
- Rollback: if decrypt failures or mismatch signals exceed thresholds, disable cutover and return to prior key version (still supported by dual-read as needed).

4) Evidence customers expect (auditor-friendly)
Minimum evidence set requested repeatedly:
- Who approved rotation (names/roles) + date/time
- What changed (key identifiers, key version, cutover flags/config) + where (env/region)
- When it changed (timestamps)
- Proof the system used the new key for writes after cutover
- Proof the system could still decrypt historical data during the dual-read window
- Confirmation old key version was not deleted prematurely (and disable timing)
- Any incidents during rotation, mitigations, and post-rotation verification checklist sign-off

Documentation deliverables required (customer-facing unless noted)
A) “Key rotation procedure” page
- Audience: Private operators + Dedicated/Hosted security reviewers
- Must include:
  - Preconditions (permissions, backups/rollback readiness, change window)
  - Step-by-step workflow (staged rollout, dual-decrypt window, cutover)
  - Verification checklist (health endpoints/dashboards, sample decrypt/read test)
  - Rollback procedure with explicit triggers
  - Expected timelines (typical dual-read window length; recommended burn-in)
  - Notes on failure modes (KMS throttling/outage) and how the system degrades

B) Evidence checklist + rotation log template
- A single page/checklist plus a copy-pastable log template customers can store in their GRC system.
- Should map to SOC 2 / ISO style narratives (“change management”, “key management”, “logging and monitoring”).
- Should be easy to generate from:
  - Redwood audit logs (including rotation events)
  - Installer validation report (Private)
  - Dashboard snapshots (KMS latency/errors, decrypt failures)

C) Private deployment operator guide: KMS integration
- Audience: customer platform/security teams running Redwood Private
- Must include:
  - Supported clouds (AWS/GCP/Azure) patterns
  - Least-privilege IAM guidance (runtime decrypt vs rotation role separation)
  - Installer preflight validation and how to interpret errors
  - Troubleshooting matrix (AccessDenied, NotFound, Throttling, Timeout, KeyDisabled)

D) Short enterprise FAQ (Sales/SE enablement)
- “What cadence do you support?”
- “Who performs rotation in Private vs Hosted?”
- “What happens if KMS is down?”
- “Can we use HSM-backed keys?”
- “How do we get audit evidence?”

Non-goals / out of scope
- Changing cryptographic primitives/algorithms.
- Redesigning broader auth or secrets management beyond KMS integration + operational docs.

Acceptance criteria
- Product-approved, consistent statements for cadence + responsibility split (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) are documented and shared with Sales/SE.
- Docs deliverables A–D above are published (or have committed publish dates + owners).
- Evidence checklist includes explicit mapping to where artifacts come from (audit logs, dashboards, installer report, ticket approvals).
- Exception path is documented and includes required compensating controls + approvers.

comments: 2025-10-30 (Naomi Feldman): Pulled recurring questions from Acme + Northpeak pre-reads. Biggest gap is not technical capability—it’s proving the process is repeatable + auditable. Need standard “evidence packet” that doesn’t require Security to join every call.

2025-11-04 (Olga Petrov): For SOC2/ISO narratives, make sure we capture: approver identity, change ticket ID, and exported audit log entries. Screenshots are fine but auditors prefer machine-exported logs. Recommend including explicit field names customers can search for in audit export (event type, actor, key ARN/URI, environment).

2025-11-07 (Elliot Price): Docs can publish two pages in the docs site: “KMS integration (Private)” and “Key rotation procedure + evidence checklist”. Need final wording on cadence (“at least annually; quarterly recommended”) and who executes rotation for Dedicated (contract-dependent).

2025-11-12 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE side, we should state clear rollback triggers in customer-facing docs (e.g., decrypt failure rate threshold, sustained KMS timeout rate). Also include guidance that aggressive retry settings are disallowed by default; helps explain why system may fail fast rather than hang.

2025-11-18 (Naomi Feldman): Marking done—statements finalized and handed to Docs/Sales Enablement. Publishing tracked via docs PRs and ENG tickets. Follow-up: once audit-log exporter includes rotation events by default, update FAQ to mention SIEM ingestion without manual exports.
